ground_truth.description: The new __init__.py guidance states as a blanket rule that for cross_project findings 'cite_task is the sole dedup anchor there', but the stage2.py section it cross-references defines two sub-cases: only sub-case (1) (a local task is the subject) has a cite_task anchor; in sub-case (2) (work lives entirely in the unknown target project) cite_task returns unknown_project and attaches nothing, so the finding is deduped by its normalised description — not by cite_task. The summary overgeneralizes and can mislead the recon agent for the target-project-only case.

The change's only edit to fused-memory/tests/test_stages.py deletes one trailing blank line at end of file; it is unrelated to the task (a prompt fix) and is pure diff noise. The file still ends with a blank line afterwards.

The LLM-facing prompt text now names private Python implementation symbols (_derive_affected_ids, compute_content_fingerprint) in the new unknown-target cross_project sub-case (stage2.py:119-129) and in the shared _RECON_REPORT_TOOL_GUIDANCE used by Stages 1-3 (__init__.py:87-95), restating the fingerprint mechanism a second/third time inside one long run-on bullet. The model cannot act on the names, they cost tokens every run, and a rename of those functions silently makes the prompt stale with no gate catching it; the behavioural rule (cite the local subject task so the finding is recognised across cycles) would suffice.

No test pins the new instruction in STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT's unknown-target cross_project branch (cite_task the LOCAL subject task with the local project_id), nor the behaviour it relies on (a task_id=None cross_project finding citing a task in the cycle's own project gets a cited_tasks entry and a description-independent compute_content_fingerprint). A later prompt edit could drop sub-case (1), or reword it to cite the target project, with every test still green; the only test-file change is a whitespace deletion.

The rewritten '# Dedup anchor' comment block (__init__.py:68-76) restates nearly verbatim the _RECON_REPORT_TOOL_GUIDANCE string directly below it, and the same mechanism is described again in stage2.py's Cross-Project Routing section, so three prose copies must be kept in sync (the prior copy already drifted, which is what this task corrected). It also carries change-history provenance ('corrected task-1594') that belongs in the commit message.

The rewritten shared report-tool guidance (used in the Stage 1, 2 and 3 system prompts) describes only the escalation-fingerprint dedup path (_derive_affected_ids -> compute_content_fingerprint, which reads cited_* lists and never the top-level task_id) and then calls top-level task_id a 'supplementary stable anchor' for multi-task findings whose cited_tasks signature shifts, implying it stabilises that fingerprint, which it does not. It drops the previously true statement that the flag-dedup path (flag_dedup.compute_flag_signature, used for cross-cycle Stage 1 flag markers and in-run (task_id, flag_type) dedup in recon_report.add_finding) prefers the top-level task_id and uses sorted cited_tasks only as a fallback. The guidance therefore misattributes which anchor feeds which dedup mechanism.

The new sub-case (1) tells the LLM 'The local task's project_id IS in "Known Projects" (this cycle is bound to it)', but TaskKnowledgeSync._format_known_projects_section returns '' when fewer than two projects are known, so in a single-project deployment the payload has no Known Projects section, while the same prompt section says cite_task only records citations for project_ids listed in Known Projects. cite_task itself succeeds (ReconReportState.known_projects includes the primary root), but the prompt's stated precondition contradicts what the model sees and may lead it to skip the local citation.

The task asked only for a Stage 2 Cross-Project Routing prompt change, but the diff also rewrites _RECON_REPORT_TOOL_GUIDANCE, which is interpolated into the Stage 1 and Stage 3 system prompts as well, changing the dedup-anchor instructions all three stages receive without the task record or commit stating that cross-stage effect.

Sub-case (1) instructs Stage 2 to cite_task the local subject task 'even when it is being re-scoped or cancelled', and the next bullet permits deleting such a local task, but nothing says to cite before deleting. ReconReportState.cite_task looks the task up via get_task and returns task_not_found (appending nothing) when it no longer exists, so a delete-then-cite order silently loses the anchor and the finding falls back to description-only dedup.

task.title: Fix stage2.py STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT cross_project section to instruct cite_task for cross_project findings
task.description: The cross_project section of STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT (~L100-106 in stage2.py) does not instruct Stage 2 to call cite_task when emitting cross_project findings. This means cross_project findings have empty cited_tasks → _derive_affected_ids returns [] → compute_content_fingerprint hashes only the drifting description text → the finding re-escalates every reconciliation cycle without being folded by the cross-cycle dedup machinery. The fix (task 1573) landed compute_flag_signature falling back to cited_tasks[0].task_id, but only works when Stage 2 actually attaches citations. Without the prompt instruction, Stage 2 never does.
task.details: Fix: update the STAGE2_SYSTEM_PROMPT Cross-Project Routing section to include an explicit instruction like: 'When emitting a cross_project finding, always call cite_task(finding_id, project_id, task_id) for the local task whose scope has been rerouted, even when that task_id is the source task being re-scoped or cancelled. This provides the task_id anchor that compute_content_fingerprint needs to fold duplicate findings cross-cycle.' Also verify the instruction is present in the actual cross_project routing guidance paragraph so future Stage 2 runs inherit it. See memory cfe9adc3 for the gap analysis.
